narrative:
The model estimates a 69% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of just 1-5 years was the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expects to stay, only about half have this same low level of experience, while many others have 6 or more years. This limited background appears to signal higher turnover risk to the system.

The fact that you have received other job offers while working here was the second most important driver, pushing the prediction toward you eventually leaving. Most employees the model predicts will stay do not receive such external opportunities.

Your employment in the "other" sector, rather than medical or education, was the third strongest influence and also nudged the outcome toward leaving. Only about 22% of employees expected to stay work in this broader category.

While several positive elements exist in your profile, such as receiving a bonus, having no overtime, and living close to work, these were not enough to outweigh the top factors. The organization should discuss your career development goals with you and explore ways to strengthen your long-term commitment. You may wish to reflect on whether the external opportunities you are receiving better align with your aspirations.
